prompt: Prepare an RFP for leftover torch-applied waterproofing subcontract. Write the invitation letter, scope of works, prequalification criteria, evaluation method, and key dates in full paragraphs.
answer:
**INVITATION LETTER**

[Employer / Principal Contractor Letterhead]

Date: [Insert Date]

To: Prospective Tenderers

Subject: Invitation to Tender — Leftover Torch-Applied Waterproofing Subcontract for **Prod Construction UI Aug 22**

We hereby invite your organisation to submit a tender for the leftover torch-applied waterproofing works for the above-referenced project. The subcontract comprises the supply, installation, testing, and protection of waterproofing membrane in strict accordance with the Khor Waterproofing Specification (unique document token **KHOR-WP-SPEC-TOKEN-33107**). Key technical parameters mandated under this specification include a **4mm torch-applied SBS** membrane with minimum **laps of 100mm**, together with a mandatory **hold point before backfill** that requires **Engineer witness** and formal acceptance prior to any covering works. Enclosed with this invitation are the Scope of Works, Prequalification Criteria, Evaluation Method, and Key Dates, which form an integral part of this RFP. Your tender shall be submitted in a sealed envelope, clearly marked “Tender for Leftover Torch-Applied Waterproofing — Prod Construction UI Aug 22,” and delivered to [Insert Address] no later than [Insert Time] on [Insert Submission Deadline Date]. The Employer reserves the right to reject any or all tenders and to waive minor informalities without incurring liability.

---

**SCOPE OF WORKS**

The subcontractor shall furnish all labour, supervision, plant, equipment, tools, materials, temporary works, personal protective equipment, and consumables necessary to execute and complete the leftover torch-applied waterproofing in full compliance with Khor Waterproofing Specification (unique document token **KHOR-WP-SPEC-TOKEN-33107**). The membrane shall be **4mm torch-applied SBS**, installed with side and end **laps of 100mm**, and all preparatory works—including substrate cleaning, priming, detailing at penetrations, corners, and terminations—shall be completed to the standard required to achieve the Engineer’s acceptance. A critical **inspection hold point before backfill** applies to every completed section; the subcontractor shall programme the works so that no backfill is placed until the Engineer has inspected and witnessed the membrane installation and issued written acceptance. The scope further includes the supply and installation of any specified protection boards, temporary guarding of completed work, safe handling and storage of propane cylinders and torching equipment, removal of waste and off-cuts, and close coordination with the excavation, concrete foundation, and backfill trades to ensure the hold point is accessible at the agreed milestone. The subcontractor shall submit detailed method statements, risk assessments, and material data sheets for review no less than seven calendar days prior to commencing any hot-works on site.

---

**PREQUALIFICATION CRITERIA**

To be considered for award, tenderers must demonstrate not less than five years of continuous and proven experience in the supply and installation of torch-applied SBS waterproofing membranes on building or civil-engineering projects of comparable scale and complexity, evidenced by completion certificates, final account statements, or client references that can be verified. Tenderers must possess valid commercial registration and specialty waterproofing trade licences for the jurisdiction in which the project is located, and must employ site personnel who hold current training certification in hot-applied bituminous membrane installation and propane hot-work safety. Financial capacity shall be demonstrated through audited financial statements for the last two fiscal years or, where audited statements are unavailable, through irrevocable bank references and bond lines confirming the ability to fund the works through to final acceptance. Tenderers must also submit evidence of comprehensive general liability, employer’s liability, and works-insurance coverage appropriate to hot-work operations. A satisfactory safety record is required, supported by a three-year incident history and, where available, ISO 45001 or equivalent occupational health and safety management certification. In addition, tenderers must confirm ownership or assured long-term lease of torching equipment, a reliable supply chain for 4mm SBS membrane compatible with the specification, and sufficient uncommitted supervisory and labour resources to complete the works within the programme without detriment to the hold-point and backfill sequence. Joint-venture bids are permissible only if a single lead partner is identified and joint and several liability is confirmed in the submission.

---

**EVALUATION METHOD**

Tenders will be evaluated on a quality-and-price basis to determine the most economically advantageous offer.
